investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:56–10:04Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pod remained Unschedulable for 122–143 seconds until the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the remote agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — the four required evidence fields defined in the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new agent pod.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making the cluster effectively a 2-node pool for this workload class.
[Possible] Peer-pod node pool under-provisioned for current load: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote agents than is currently being requested across all tenants.
[Possible] Leaked or zombie agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations: previously created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up may be holding resource slots, preventing new scheduling.

[Lower confidence] Node affinity configuration drift: the pod's node selector or affinity rules may have been tightened or the node labels on the 4 non-matching nodes may have changed, reducing the eligible node pool from a larger set to just 2 nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:56–10:04Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pod remained Unschedulable for 122–143 seconds until the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the remote agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — the four required evidence fields defined in the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making the cluster effectively a 2-node pool for this workload class.
[Possible] Peer-pod node pool under-provisioned for current load: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote agents than is currently being requested across all tenants.
[Possible] Leaked or zombie agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations: previously created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up may be holding resource slots, preventing new scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner could not create a remote agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever produced, causing the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on its 2 peer-pod-capable nodes. Every attempt to schedule a new remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) timed out waiting for the pod to become schedulable, and the check returned a failure before any runtime evidence could be collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval-created pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so even if VM capacity were freed, the other 4 nodes could not accept the pod. This is a configuration constraint that narrows the schedulable pool to exactly those 2 exhausted nodes.

TERTIARY — a resource leak or runaway workload holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if a prior eval run or user session left agent pods running without cleanup, those pods would hold VM slots and prevent new scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 is intended to prevent this, but a failed or interrupted prior run may have bypassed cleanup.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have a VM quota that is too small for concurrent eval and production workloads, causing contention during peak usage. No traffic or quota data is present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.
